source: William Lilly Christian Astrology 1647 first edition Wellcome b30338724 original frames PDF583–585
role_scope: Mature-age fullness/leanness as historic conditional astrological descriptions, not actual anthropometric/clinical predictions
cautions: Do not convert 'first/latter part' into a particular degree bound without source proof.
Do not infer medical/metabolic state or body mass from these historical claims.
Preserve all sign-position reversals, partile aspects, equal-dominion tiebreakers, Mars-absence and joint conditions.
Printed folio sequence 549/542/543/552 is incorrect but image text sequence is continuous.

source_groups.source_group: Printed chapter CXII heading and mature-age definition

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXII Of the grossenesse or leannesse of Bodies
claims.historical_meaning: A separate numbered chapter begins below the divider on original PDF583 and treats body bulk or leanness rather than height alone.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: after a full age
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly explicitly limits this judgment to constitution after mature adulthood, not body size in childhood.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or about thirty yeers, or somewhat after
claims.historical_meaning: The source supplies an approximate age of thirty years or later rather than a fixed numerical threshold.

source_groups.source_group: Primary Ascendant sign, ruler, and dignity selection

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: judgment ... from the Signe ascending and his Lord
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly names the Ascendant sign and its ruler as the principal references for mature body build.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: that Planet who hath most dignities therein
claims.historical_meaning: The planet with the greatest dignities in the rising sign is used in the selection procedure; a method for ties appears later.

source_groups.source_group: First sign group: Aries Taurus Leo

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Aries Taurus Leo first part declare grossenesse
claims.historical_meaning: Aries, Taurus and Leo are assigned larger body build for the earlier portion of the sign, according to the text; not observed height/weight.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the latter part leannesse
claims.historical_meaning: The latter portions of Aries, Taurus and Leo receive the opposite slimmer-build prediction; retain sign position as essential.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Gemini Scorpio ... first part ... leannesse
claims.historical_meaning: Gemini and Scorpio are assigned lean build in their earlier sign portions.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the latter grossenesse
claims.historical_meaning: Gemini and Scorpio are assigned fuller build in the later sign portions, reversing their early-position judgment.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Cancer Capricorn ... first part mediocrity
claims.historical_meaning: Cancer and Capricorn in the earlier portion are alleged to imply middle build tending lean rather than simply thin.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: latter part tending more to grossenesse
claims.historical_meaning: The later portions of Cancer and Capricorn are alleged to incline toward fuller build.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Sagittarius ... first part leane
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly makes the earlier Sagittarius section a lean-build claim.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: the latter part grossenesse
claims.historical_meaning: The later portion of Sagittarius is assigned greater fullness; without a frozen split this is not executable.

source_groups.source_group: Four moderate-build signs and Aquarius exception

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Aquarius Pisces Libra Virgo ... moderate proportion
claims.historical_meaning: Aquarius, Pisces, Libra and Virgo are grouped as having moderate body proportions, rather than two opposed halves.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: latter part of Aquarius declines to leannesse
claims.historical_meaning: The text modifies the general moderate rule by making late Aquarius incline leaner; record this explicit exception separately.

source_groups.source_group: Partile aspect selection and alternate sign-of-ruler

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the ascendant ... behold the degree ascending partilly
claims.historical_meaning: If the Ascendant ruler has a partile aspect to the rising degree, the judgment follows the nature of the Ascendant sign.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if it be not so ... Signe the Lord of the ascendant is in
claims.historical_meaning: When that partile criterion does not hold, Lilly redirects judgment to the zodiac sign containing the Ascendant ruler.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: so that he be in any aspect with a Planet
claims.historical_meaning: The preceding alternate-ruler-sign case is expressly qualified by its aspect to another planet; do not omit the condition.

source_groups.source_group: No-planet-partile fallback to an unoccupied sign half

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the ascendant beheld by no Planet partilly
claims.historical_meaning: The author adds a further fallback when no planet partile-aspects the Ascendant ruler.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: judge by that mediety ... Almuten doth not occupie
claims.historical_meaning: The specified fallback uses the half of the sign not occupied by the Almuten; the wording is unusually counterintuitive and needs expert interpretation before software encoding.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of House or Exaltation ... joyned to the Sun
claims.historical_meaning: The domicile or exaltation ruler of the Ascendant is considered in a conjunction with the Sun for a larger-body prediction.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: within the moyity of Orbs (Mars being absent)
claims.historical_meaning: The Sun–ruler configuration requires orb-moiety proximity and Mars's absence, both essential constraints.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if the Signe ascending and Lord ... consent
claims.historical_meaning: The claimed fuller body depends additionally on agreement from the Ascendant sign and its ruler; the source does not define an algorithm for agreement.

source_groups.source_group: Equal-dominion tie breaker and cross reference

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: If two Planets have equall dominion in the Horoscope
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly explicitly anticipates tied planetary authority instead of letting the reader select a favorite result.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: him that doth most partilly cast his aspect
claims.historical_meaning: Within a tie, the planet forming the more partile aspect to the Ascendant is given priority.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: preferre him that hath the house before ... Exaltation
claims.historical_meaning: Domicile rulership wins over exaltation when adjudicating a remaining priority conflict.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: reference to the first part of the Introduction
claims.historical_meaning: The author's discussion refers readers to earlier Book I descriptions of planetary natural shape and form; this is a cross-reference, not independent validation.

source_groups.source_group: Explicit omission and historical disability language

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Some have treated of Monsters ... I forbeare
claims.historical_meaning: Lilly explicitly declines to judge a historical category of bodily atypicality he calls 'Monsters'; the term is archaic and harmful and must not be used as a present-day diagnostic label.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: belong not to the naturall course of Heaven
claims.historical_meaning: The rationale separates exceptional natural phenomena from what he claims can be interpreted in ordinary astrology; the omission must not be filled in speculatively.

source_groups.source_group: Following printed chapter CXIII general fortune: boundary only

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXIII Of the generall Fortune or Misery of the Native
claims.historical_meaning: Printed CXIII/editorial CXIV opens at the top of source frame585; it is a separate subject about generalized good/bad fortune.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Having well considered the Geniture
claims.historical_meaning: Only the start of the next chapter is witnessed here, not admitted as an assessed rule in the mature body-size chapter.
